applepay.notes: Global: Apple Pay in Singapore is a token of the same card. Most issuers only give a blanket 'same rewards as physical card' statement. Explicit carve-outs exist only for Citi Rewards (mobile wallet excluded from online bonus, both in-app and Safari web checkout) and HSBC Revolution (Apple Pay named as qualifying contactless). Engine method mapping: applepay_instore is treated as physical_tap for earn unless a perCard entry says otherwise; applepay_inapp covers in-app and Safari web. Layered paths: Amaze over Apple Pay is treated as Amaze (layerVia ['applepay']). Wallet top-ups (GrabPay, EZ-Link, SimplyGo) are excluded on HSBC Revolution, Amex, Maybank XL and Chocolate; that is a stored-value rule, not an Apple Pay rule. Kris+ accepts only Apple Pay or Google Pay.

supported.note: HSBC lists all primary and supplementary HSBC credit and debit cards in good standing, excluding corporate cards. The page does not name Revolution or Visa, but Revolution is a standard retail card.

inStore.note: Apple Pay is named inside the Selected Contactless Payments definition (T&C eff. 1 Apr 2026, cl.5). Bonus still needs an eligible MCC (cl.7). Inserting the chip card is NOT contactless, so tap physical card and Apple Pay are equivalent but insert is not.

inApp.note: Re-researched 1 Nov 2026: HSBC T&C cl.6 treats a transaction as online if the merchant or acquirer processes it as an online transaction type. In-app and web Apple Pay are processed as card-not-present e-commerce, so they should carry the online indicator. No HSBC wording and no confirmed data point found (MileLion reader question unanswered; Suitesmile Mar 2026 names Apple Pay only as contactless). Kept as online, inferred.

supported.note: Applies to all HSBC credit cards in good standing; TravelOne not named.

inStore.note: 'Same rewards and privileges as your physical HSBC Card'. TravelOne T&C (31 Mar 2025) has no channel or wallet clause; earn depends on currency and spend only, so tap, insert and Apple Pay in store earn identically.

inApp.note: No channel tier on this card, so in-app Apple Pay earns the same as any other spend. 'online' is used only because the enum has no 'same as physical' value for inApp.

supported.note: Cardmember's Agreement cl.10.11 covers cards provisioned in third-party digital wallets and tokenised cards. No Citi Singapore page naming Apple Pay found; Apple Pay with Citi Mastercard is treated as routine by MileLion and Mainly Miles.

inStore.note: Brian confirms in-store Apple Pay earns the bonus at whitelisted MCCs.

inApp.note: Online bonus excludes 'mobile wallet' transactions; online means 'the internet or mobile applications' (s8 cl.6(ii) and footnote). Both in-app and Safari web Apple Pay checkout are therefore base (0.4 mpd). Paying with the card directly in the app earns 4 mpd. Kris+ accepts only Apple Pay or Google Pay so earns 0.4 mpd. Amaze with Citi behind it is not caught by this exclusion (see layers.amaze).
